analysis.title: 2026 RBC Capital Markets Global Technology, Internet, Media and Telecommunications Conference – Updates from Day 2
key_insights: Cloudflare (NET) is RBC's favorite long-term idea. Q3 revenue grew 31% vs 28% the prior quarter. The Workers developer base crossed 10M, about 30% of the Internet sits behind its network after adding 5% last quarter, and GAAP profitability is now expected in Q4/26. Rated Outperform.

Cloudflare's Q3 beat of about 6% was the largest in recent history and the full-year raise was the largest ever in dollars. Management said investors should not extrapolate a 6% beat and aims for the 10-quarter average of slightly above 3%. cRPO grew 37% and Q3 was the biggest ACV quarter ever. CJ Desai announced his departure for a CEO role.

Datadog (DDOG): RBC sees post-Q3 weakness as a buying opportunity. Q3 revenue grew +35.2%, a 4.4% beat. Q4 revenue growth excluding the largest customer would have been low-to-mid 30% vs 25.4% guidance. RBC's own math (not validated by management) implies OpenAI revenue in Q4 guidance is down nearly 70% y/y, and OpenAI could be below 1.5% of revenue next year.

Datadog's flat sequential Q4 revenue guide partly reflects a wave of early renewals, where customers took volume- and term-based discounts for larger, longer commitments. Customers historically grow past the new commit in about a quarter, so late-Q4 and Q1/27 should benefit. Infrastructure monitoring crossed $2B ARR.

F5 (FFIV): RBC thinks the selloff after Q4 results is overdone. FY/26 revenue grew about 13% and product revenue 23%. FY/27 guidance is 8-9% revenue growth, which RBC sees as conservative with upside to consensus in the low double digits. Direct AI bookings exceeded $100M in FY/26, up nearly 300% y/y. Rated Outperform.

Celestica (CLS): FY27 revenue guidance of $40B (+90% y/y) includes only awarded programs, and customer demand exceeds that level. Growth is gated by supply and execution. FCF is expected to be negative in FY27 and turn positive in FY28. RBC sees compelling risk-reward after the valuation de-rating. Rated Outperform.

Celestica has ten 1.6T switch program wins (six scale-out, four scale-up) and a CPO switch win with a hyperscaler. It has new multi-billion-dollar programs with OpenAI and AMD, with the OpenAI ramp weighted to 2H FY27. It plans over $300MM of R&D in FY27.

Cisco (not covered): product order growth of 21% in Q1/27 understates demand because only orders shipping within 90 days count, and hyperscaler orders beyond that go to unreported backlog. Firewall orders have grown 30%+ for three consecutive quarters, and security grew 7% in Q1/27. AI infrastructure is a gross margin headwind as its mix rises. No scale-up product has been announced, and scale-up revenue in FY/27 would be surprising.

Google read-through (GOOGL): panelists said AI Mode monetization is lagging because Google is prioritizing user adoption, with the fix likely from better measurement and attribution as AI Mode inventory is folded into existing campaign types. Early chatbot ad underperformance was seen as an ad product problem, not a user intent problem. RBC came away constructive on Google's ability to monetize AI surfaces.

The agentic advertising panel (Apostra's Brian O'Kelley) argued agents can do intermediary ad tech functions at a 0% take rate, leaving commodity ad tech most exposed. The panelist sees a manageable 5-10% headwind for Google and Meta, and a larger opportunity for Snap, Reddit, Pinterest, ChatGPT and local broadcasters.

Nasdaq (NDAQ): the Index business grew 39% in Q3 with $141bn of net inflows over the trailing twelve months. Capital Markets Tech ARR grew 19% and RegTech about 15%. 23/5 trading goes live December 6. The Nasdaq equity token with Kraken targets a first-half 2027 launch and is not expected to be a material revenue source. Share repurchases are $1.2bn over nine months, with about $1.5bn targeted for 2026. Rated Outperform.

Axon (AXON): the company elected to settle the roughly $1.2B Skydio investment about 90% in cash instead of the original 60% cash and 40% stock, because it did not want to issue equity at current prices. FY26 FCF is guided to $350-400M (about 40% conversion). Memory and component costs cut 2026 gross margin by about 50 bps. RBC expects about 25%+ revenue growth and says ALPR is under 1% of sales. Rated Outperform.

TD SYNNEX (SNX): management expects FCF in Q4/26, and Hyve's FCF yield to improve materially in FY27. A large AI server program diluted Hyve margins and is expected to lap in Q4/26. PC units are expected to decline mid-to-high single digits in Q4/26, with ASP increases more than offsetting. Rated Outperform.

Astera Labs (ALAB): management gave no update to the near-term outlook. RBC estimates content per XPU is about $1,000 today and sees a path to $2,000+ in next-generation platforms. Scale-up optical is on track for 2H27/2028 and CXL for an initial ramp in 2H27. Gross margin and operating margin are expected to stay near the 70% and 40% target model. Rated Outperform.

IBM: virtualization bookings are above $800M, and management said it has driven $5.5B of cost savings over four years through internal AI. Lightwell, an open-source security offering, has 50K packages available. RBC rates IBM Outperform.

Pegasystems (PEGA): RBC is incrementally positive on pipeline strength and new logos, saying the Q4 pipeline is the strongest ever. RBC remains cautious on a meaningful reacceleration in ACV growth because close rates and 2027 budgets are hard to predict. Rated Outperform.

Lower-rated names: N-able (Sector Perform) expects CY/27 to be a building year with cc ARR growth around 5%. Gartner (Sector Perform) sees contract value pressure from federal anniversary effects and Middle East exposure of about 3-4% of CV, and RBC says softer CV growth could weigh on 2027 revenue and margins. Fastly, NetScout, ADP, Clarivate and First Advantage are also Sector Perform.

Magnite (MGNI): CTV grew 39% in Q3 with top-10 accounts growing in the mid-40s. DV+ is stabilizing and the DOJ's behavioral remedies in the Google case came out largely as Magnite hoped, though the final ruling is pending and not built into FY/27 expectations. Rated Outperform.

PicS (PICS): management said credit quality is not deteriorating and expects 90+ day NPLs to normalize at about 9% in 2Q27 after the change to its unsecured write-off policy. The KEV acquisition had a lower-than-expected earnings contribution and is expected to be accretive in FY27. Rated Outperform.

Private companies: Snyk is a mid-$300M ARR business with Evo attaching to 50%+ of the business at a 15% premium. CodeRabbit grew ARR from $10M to $100M in 14 months and raised a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation in August 2026. Aaru was valued around $1B in a late-2025 Series A, per TechCrunch.

market_movers.rationale: Favorite long-term idea. Q3 revenue growth accelerated to 31%, with Workers, agentic traffic and security tailwinds.
Tier 1 AI winner, with post-Q3 weakness seen as a buying opportunity. Core growth is masked by an early renewal wave and the large-customer headwind.
Selloff after Q4 results is overdone. FY/27 guidance of 8-9% growth looks conservative against an upward bias to consensus.
FY27 revenue guidance of $40B covers awarded programs only. Valuation has re-rated lower while visibility is strong.
More comfort on positioning after the keynote, covering open source, Red Hat, Lightwell, AI and quantum.
Broad-based demand across segments from GenAI and always-on markets, with Index inflows strong.
Greater confidence in 25%+ revenue growth, 2028 targets and margin expansion.
Distribution and Hyve both expected to generate FCF over time, with Hyve margins stabilizing after the AI server program laps.
Strong pipeline and new logo momentum, offset by caution on ACV reacceleration.
Non-big-4 education markets growing about 30%. Gross margin decline is mix-driven, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding.
VCP momentum with 35 customers signed, and payments attach expanding beyond restaurants.
Management sees NPLs normalizing at about 9% in 2Q27, and private payroll loan share at about 7.3%.
Path to content per XPU doubling to $2,000+, with margins staying in the target range.
CTV at an inflection with 39% Q3 growth, DV+ stabilizing.
Enterprise adoption, CTV and mobile in-app driving revenue acceleration and margin expansion.
Targets low-double-digit revenue growth and mid-teens EPS growth, with custom indexing growing 20-30%.
Constructive on Google's ability to monetize AI surfaces over time despite a lag in AI Mode monetization.
PEO pay per control growth below 1%, FY27 margin expansion guided 70-90 bps.
Softer contract value growth could weigh on 2027 revenue, and analyst hiring is a margin headwind.
Stable demand, disposals nearly done, organic growth expected to improve in 2027.
Base growth of 4%, 29.3% adjusted EBITDA margin in 3Q26, on track for the 31-32% margin target by 2028.
Security growth of about 32% seen as sustainable, FY29 revenue target of $1.1B-$1.3B.
1H/27 revenue grew 6.6% y/y with a strong 2H pipeline, though service provider spending is lumpy.
CY/27 framed as a building year with cc ARR growth around 5%.

sector_views.rationale: RBC calls Cloudflare, Datadog, IBM and others AI beneficiaries, and sees AI adoption driving observability, security and edge platform demand.
AI Mode and chatbot ad monetization lag is seen as temporary. Agentic AI could pressure commodity ad tech and shift some spend away from Google and Meta.
Hyperscaler demand exceeds supply at Celestica, Cisco says reported orders understate demand, and Astera sees content per XPU doubling.

earnings_insights: Cloudflare Q3 (reported): revenue +31% y/y vs +28% the prior quarter. The beat was about 6% vs guidance. cRPO grew 37%. Management guides closer to the pin, aiming for the 10-quarter average beat of slightly above 3%.

Datadog Q3 (reported): revenue +35.2%, a 4.4% beat vs +35.6% and 4.0% the prior quarter. Non-AI-natives grew in the high-20%s. Q4 guidance implies flat sequential revenue, with Q4 growth excluding the largest customer at low-to-mid 30% vs 25.4% guided.
F5 FY/26 (reported): revenue growth about 13%, product revenue +23%. FY/27 guidance (company guide) is 8-9% revenue growth, and RBC expects upside to consensus in the low double digits.
Celestica FY27 (company guidance): $40B revenue, +90% y/y, awarded programs only. Negative FCF expected in FY27 and positive in FY28.
Cisco Q1/27 (reported): product order growth of 21%, security growth of 7% vs an initial expectation of low single digits, firewall orders +30% for three consecutive quarters.
Magnite Q3 (reported): CTV +39%, top-10 accounts growing in the mid-40s, political ad spend 2x the presidential cycle and 4x the midterm cycle.
Nasdaq Q3 (reported): Index business +39%, Capital Markets Tech ARR +19%, RegTech ARR about +15%. Verafin signed 12 enterprise clients YTD through 3Q26 vs 9 in all of 2025.
First Advantage 3Q26 (reported): base revenue +4% (1% in 1Q26, 2% in 2Q26), adjusted EBITDA margin 29.3%, 14 enterprise wins vs 20 in 2Q26. FY26 FCF just under about $200M.

ADP 1Q27 (reported): client float income grew about 15%, PPC growth 2%. FY27 guidance (company guide): ES pricing 130-140 bps, margin expansion 70-90 bps, client balances +4-5%, blended yield about 3.8%.
Clarivate 3Q26 (reported): organic ACV growth +1.8%, up 30 bps, adjusted EBITDA margin about 45%. FY27 guidance: FCF growth 10-15%, net leverage target of about 3.5x.
N-able 3Q26: repurchased about 10.2M shares for $38.7M. CY/26 unlevered FCF guidance (company guide) of $116-118M.
Axon FY26 guidance (company guide): FCF of $350-400M, about 40% conversion. 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin roughly flat vs 2026, not formal guidance.
NetScout 1H/27 (reported): revenue +6.6% y/y, toward the high end of the full-year mid-single-digit outlook.
PicS 3Q26 (reported): first payment defaults of 7.8%, improved from the prior quarter. Management expects 90+ day NPLs to normalize at about 9% in 2Q27.
Fastly Q3 (reported): security growth about 32% y/y, with sequential growth above 7% for four straight quarters.
Datadog is comparing Q4 against a base where overage from the largest customer inflated the third quarter, so RBC says the Q4 upside should be measured excluding that overage.
crypto_views: Nasdaq is developing the Nasdaq equity token with Kraken, targeting launch in the first half of 2027. It lets issuers represent listed equity on a blockchain while keeping access to U.S. liquidity. Management does not expect material revenue near term and is open to other chains and non-exclusive arrangements.
Nasdaq's surveillance business added Kalshi and Kraken as clients, as prediction markets and digital asset firms seek integrity frameworks.
Flywire supports stablecoin and fiat payments through its BVNK partnership. Volumes are small and the spreads it captures are comparable between the two rails.
Cloudflare is building Wallet and Monetization Gateway so agents can transact on a user's behalf, positioning for agentic commerce.
risk_factors: Cloudflare: management warns against extrapolating the 6% Q3 beat, and CFO CJ Desai is departing for a CEO role.
Datadog: concentration in its largest customer (OpenAI) and an early renewal wave that is a short-term headwind to Q4 revenue.
Celestica: FY27 growth requires heavy working capital and capex, leading to negative FCF in FY27. Growth is gated by supply and execution.
Cisco: AI infrastructure mix is a gross margin headwind, and tougher y/y comparisons are ahead.
Axon: ALPR faces public and legislative scrutiny with a period of uncertainty expected, and memory and component costs reduce gross margin about 50 bps in 2026.
Gartner: elongated sales cycles, Middle East exposure, and margin pressure if contract value does not reaccelerate.
Pegasystems: close rates and 2027 budgets are hard to predict, limiting ACV reacceleration.
Ad tech: agentic AI disintermediation could hit commodity digital surfaces and intermediaries, and AI Mode monetization may lag longer than expected for Google.
PicS: NPL normalization depends on the aging of the credit portfolio, and Nubank is becoming more aggressive in private payroll loans.
TD SYNNEX: Hyve consumes cash during program ramps, and PC units are expected to decline in Q4/26.
vol_and_positioning: F5 shares sold off after Q4 results, which RBC calls overdone. Datadog shares are weak after Q3, which RBC views as a buying opportunity.
Celestica has undergone a downward valuation re-rating, which RBC cites as a reason for compelling risk-reward.
geopolitical: Conflict in the Middle East is cited as a drag on Gartner, where Middle East customers are about 3-4% of contract value (mostly energy companies, oil companies and governments), and on First Advantage in India and parts of APAC through fuel disruptions.
Tariff and trade policy disruption have lengthened sales cycles at Gartner and increased uncertainty in healthcare.
Digital sovereignty requirements across EMEA, APCJ and regulated North American industries are driving hybrid multi-cloud architecture commitments at F5 and sovereign cloud demand at Pegasystems.

tension_points.bull_case: Panelists say the lag is temporary, with all-time-high search volumes, Google prioritizing adoption over monetization, and multi-turn ads launched this week showing active format iteration.
tension_points.bear_case: AI Mode performance improvement is not yet apparent after about 6 months. Conversational search is mid-funnel and further from purchase intent, and Google is bundling inventory and hiding search term data, limiting transparency.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued absence of monetization improvement as AI Mode inventory is folded into existing campaign types, since the panelist expects any fix to come from better measurement and attribution.

tension_points.bull_case: Agents act as closed-loop ad managers at a 0% take rate and open new channels for underpenetrated platforms like Snap, Reddit and Pinterest, with only a 5-10% headwind for Google and Meta.
tension_points.bear_case: The other panelist is bearish on autonomous decision-making agents in the near term, seeing behavior fragmenting across AI search and external validation, so a single agent experience is unlikely.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slow adoption of autonomous agents and agent-driven transactions, since protocols such as Google's A2A have not gained traction.

tension_points.bull_case: Excluding the largest customer, Q4 growth would have been low-to-mid 30% with core growth masked by early renewals, and non-AI natives accelerated to high-20%s growth.
tension_points.bear_case: RBC's math implies OpenAI revenue in Q4 guidance is down nearly 70% y/y, and the early renewal wave drives a flat sequential Q4 revenue guide.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q4 and Q1/27 results failing to show customers growing past their new commit levels within about a quarter, as management historically observes.
